ko.title: [Logistics 101 #13] 소포는 두 번 움직이고, 그 데이터는 쉰 번 움직인다.

segments.src: > Warehouses and trucks move boxes, but software decides which box, which truck, and when — and that software is really three systems (WMS, TMS, ERP) stitched together by scans.
segments.tr: > 창고와 트럭은 상자를 옮기지만, 어떤 상자를, 어떤 트럭에, 언제 실을지는 소프트웨어가 결정합니다. 그리고 그 소프트웨어는 실제로 스캔으로 이어 붙인 세 개의 시스템(WMS, TMS, ERP)입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Picture the last thing you ordered online.
segments.tr: 온라인으로 마지막에 주문한 물건을 떠올려 보세요.

segments.src: Physically, it made maybe four moves: shelf to tote, tote to box, box to trailer, trailer to your porch.
segments.tr: 실제로 물건은 아마 네 번 움직였을 겁니다. 선반에서 토트로, 토트에서 상자로, 상자에서 트레일러로, 트레일러에서 현관 앞으로.

segments.src: Digitally, it triggered dozens of transactions — an order record, an inventory allocation, a pick task, a carton label, a rate quote, a load tender, six or seven tracking scans, an invoice.
segments.tr: 디지털로는 수십 건의 트랜잭션이 발생했습니다. 주문 기록, 재고 할당, 피킹 작업, 박스 라벨, 운임 견적, 화물 입찰(load tender), 여섯 혹은 일곱 번의 배송 추적 스캔, 그리고 송장.

segments.src: That digital layer is the **logistics information system**, and in most companies it's not one product.
segments.tr: 그 디지털 계층이 **물류 정보 시스템**이며, 대부분의 기업에서 이것은 하나의 제품이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's three, each with its own job:
segments.tr: 세 개이며, 각각 고유한 역할이 있습니다.

segments.src: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)** is the system of record — the company's books.
segments.tr: **ERP(Enterprise Resource Planning, 전사적 자원 관리)**는 기록의 원천(system of record), 즉 회사의 장부입니다.

segments.src: It holds the customer order, the purchase order, the item master, the price, the general ledger.
segments.tr: 고객 주문, 구매 주문, 품목 마스터, 가격, 총계정원장을 보관합니다.

segments.src: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.
segments.tr: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics가 여기에 해당합니다.

segments.src: The ERP knows *what* was promised to whom, but it has almost no idea where any physical carton is sitting right now.
segments.tr: ERP는 *누구에게 무엇을 약속했는지*는 알지만, 지금 특정 상자가 어디에 있는지는 거의 알지 못합니다.

segments.src: **WMS (Warehouse Management System)** runs everything inside the four walls.
segments.tr: **WMS(Warehouse Management System, 창고 관리 시스템)**는 창고 벽 안의 모든 것을 운영합니다.

segments.src: It directs receiving, decides where to putaway a pallet (slotting), generates pick tasks in an efficient walk path, controls packing and cartonization, manages cycle counts, and produces the shipping label.
segments.tr: 입고를 지시하고, 파레트를 어디에 적재(putaway)할지 결정하며(슬로팅), 효율적인 이동 경로로 피킹 작업을 생성하고, 포장과 카톤화(cartonization)를 관리하며, 순환 재고 실사(cycle count)를 수행하고, 배송 라벨을 출력합니다.

segments.src: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.
segments.tr: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber가 여기에 해당합니다.

segments.src: The WMS is the only system that truly knows that SKU 44821 is in aisle 12, bin B, quantity 63.
segments.tr: WMS만이 SKU 44821이 12번 통로, B 빈에 수량 63개로 있다는 것을 실제로 알고 있습니다.

segments.src: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** takes over once freight leaves the dock — and often before.
segments.tr: **TMS(Transportation Management System, 운송 관리 시스템)**는 화물이 도크를 떠날 때 맡으며, 종종 그 전에 개입합니다.

segments.src: It rates and compares carriers, picks the mode (parcel, LTL, truckload, intermodal), consolidates small orders into one load, tenders that load to a carrier, tracks it, and audits the freight bill against the contracted rate.
segments.tr: 운송사를 비교하고 평가하며, 운송 방식(택배, LTL, 트럭 전용 운송, 복합운송)을 선택하고, 작은 주문들을 하나의 적재분으로 묶고, 그 적재분을 운송사에 입찰(tender)하고, 추적하며, 운송 청구서를 계약 요율과 대조해 감사합니다.

segments.src: Overpaying carriers is shockingly common without one; freight audit alone often pays for the software.
segments.tr: TMS가 없으면 운송사에 과다 지불하는 일이 놀라울 만큼 흔합니다. 운임 감사만으로도 소프트웨어 비용을 회수하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: The hard part isn't any single system.
segments.tr: 어려운 점은 어느 한 시스템이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's **the seams**.
segments.tr: **이음새(seam)**입니다.

segments.src: In the U.S., those seams are usually crossed one of two ways: **EDI**, the decades-old transaction-set standard (a 940 tells the warehouse to ship, a 945 confirms it shipped, a 204 tenders a load to a trucker, a 214 sends status updates back, an 856 is the advance ship notice that tells the retailer what's on the truck), or modern **APIs**, which do the same thing in near real time.
segments.tr: 미국에서 이 이음새는 보통 두 가지 방식 중 하나로 연결됩니다. 하나는 수십 년 된 트랜잭션 세트 표준인 **EDI**입니다(940은 창고에 출고를 지시하고, 945는 출고 완료를 확인하며, 204는 운송사에 화물을 입찰하고, 214는 상태 업데이트를 되돌려 보내며, 856은 리테일러에게 트럭에 실린 물품을 알려주는 사전 출하 통지입니다). 다른 하나는 같은 일을 거의 실시간으로 수행하는 최신 **API**입니다.

segments.src: A retail vendor who mis-formats an 856 gets a chargeback, not an email.
segments.tr: 856을 잘못된 형식으로 보내는 리테일 공급사는 이메일이 아니라 청구 차감(chargeback)을 받게 됩니다.

segments.src: And all of it runs on one humble input: **the scan**.
segments.tr: 그리고 이 모든 것은 하나의 소박한 입력에 기반합니다. **스캔**입니다.

segments.src: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)
segments.tr: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)

segments.src: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit
segments.tr: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit

segments.src: **Barcodes** are the workhorse.
segments.tr: **바코드**가 주력입니다.

segments.src: A UPC identifies the product; a GS1-128 label on a pallet carries an SSCC — an 18-digit serial number that acts as a "license plate" so one scan pulls up the entire contents of that pallet.
segments.tr: UPC는 제품을 식별하고, 파레트에 붙은 GS1-128 라벨은 SSCC를 담습니다. SSCC는 18자리 일련번호로, "라이선스 플레이트" 역할을 해서 한 번의 스캔으로 그 파레트의 전체 내용물을 조회할 수 있게 합니다.

segments.src: Barcodes are effectively free to print, but they need line of sight and one read at a time.
segments.tr: 바코드는 인쇄 비용이 사실상 없지만, 시야가 확보되어야 하고 한 번에 한 개씩만 읽힙니다.

segments.src: **RFID** (in retail supply chains, usually passive UHF "RAIN" RFID) flips that.
segments.tr: **RFID**(소매 공급망에서는 보통 수동형 UHF "RAIN" RFID)는 이 한계를 뒤집습니다.

segments.src: A reader can pick up hundreds of tags at once, through a cardboard box, without anyone aiming anything.
segments.tr: 리더기는 누군가 조준하지 않아도 판지 상자를 통과해 수백 개의 태그를 한 번에 읽을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Walk a handheld down a store aisle and count the inventory in minutes instead of hours.
segments.tr: 핸드헬드 리더기를 매장 통로에 대고 걸어가면 몇 시간이 걸릴 재고 조사를 몇 분 만에 끝낼 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The tradeoff is cost and physics: tags cost a few cents each at volume rather than nothing, and radio waves behave badly around metal and liquid.
segments.tr: 대가는 비용과 물리적 특성입니다. 태그는 대량 구매 시 개당 몇 센트가 들고, 전파는 금속과 액체 주변에서 제대로 작동하지 않습니다.

segments.src: That's why RFID took off first in apparel — light, non-metallic, high SKU count, and painful to count by hand — and why Walmart's expansion of its RFID tagging requirements beyond apparel starting in 2022 pushed a lot of suppliers into it.
segments.tr: 그래서 RFID는 가볍고 금속이 없으며 SKU 수가 많고 손으로 세기 괴로운 의류 분야에서 먼저 자리 잡았습니다. 2022년 월마트가 RFID 태깅 요구 사항을 의류 이외로 확대하면서 많은 공급사가 RFID를 도입하게 된 이유이기도 합니다.

segments.src: The unglamorous truth: none of this fixes bad data.
segments.tr: 평범하지만 진실은 이 어떤 것도 나쁜 데이터를 고쳐주지 않는다는 점입니다.

segments.src: If a receiver scans a pallet into the wrong bin, the WMS confidently tells a picker to walk to an empty shelf.
segments.tr: 입고 담당자가 파레트를 잘못된 빈에 스캔하면, WMS는 피커에게 빈 선반으로 걸어가라고 자신 있게 지시합니다.

segments.src: Garbage in, expensive walk out.
segments.tr: 잘못 들어간 데이터는 비싼 헛걸음이 되어 나옵니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: It's 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 오후 11시, 오하이오주 콜럼버스입니다.

segments.src: in Columbus, Ohio, and you order a $110 pair of running shoes with free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: 당신은 무료 2일 배송 조건으로 110달러짜리 러닝화를 주문합니다.

segments.src: The retailer's **ERP** captures the order and the payment.
segments.tr: 리테일러의 **ERP**가 주문과 결제를 기록합니다.

segments.src: Available-to-promise logic checks inventory and assigns it to a fulfillment center in Indiana rather than the one in Nevada — closer to you, cheaper to ship, and the shoes are actually there.
segments.tr: 가용 재고 약속 로직이 재고를 확인하고, 네바다의 물류센터 대신 인디애나의 물류센터에 재고를 할당합니다. 고객과 가깝고 배송비가 저렴하며 신발이 실제로 그곳에 있기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The **WMS** drops a pick task onto a handheld.
segments.tr: **WMS**가 핸드헬드 기기에 피킹 작업을 띄웁니다.

segments.src: A picker walks a route the system optimized, scans the shelf barcode (confirming the right location), scans the shoe box (confirming the right SKU), and drops it in a tote.
segments.tr: 피커는 시스템이 최적화한 경로를 따라 걷고, 선반 바코드를 스캔해 올바른 위치를 확인하고, 신발 상자를 스캔해 올바른 SKU를 확인한 뒤, 토트에 담습니다.

segments.src: Packing scans it again into a carton and prints a label.
segments.tr: 포장 단계에서 다시 스캔해 카톤에 담고 라벨을 출력합니다.

segments.src: Every one of those scans is the system asking "prove it" — that's how inventory records stay honest.
segments.tr: 이 스캔 하나하나는 시스템이 "증명해"라고 요구하는 것입니다. 재고 기록이 정확하게 유지되는 방식이 바로 이것입니다.

segments.src: The **TMS** — or the parcel-rating engine that plays its role — compares carriers and service levels for that ZIP code, picks one, and transmits the shipment data before the box is even on the trailer.
segments.tr: **TMS**(또는 그 역할을 맡은 택배 요금 계산 엔진)가 해당 우편번호의 운송사와 서비스 수준을 비교해 하나를 고르고, 상자가 트레일러에 실리기도 전에 배송 데이터를 전송합니다.

segments.src: That's why your tracking number goes live with "label created" while the box is still sitting in Indiana.
segments.tr: 그래서 상자가 아직 인디애나에 있는데도 추적 번호가 "라벨 생성됨" 상태로 활성화되는 것입니다.

segments.src: Overnight the trailer runs to a sort hub — Memphis, Louisville, wherever the network routes it.
segments.tr: 밤사이 트레일러는 분류 허브로 이동합니다. 멤피스든 루이빌이든, 네트워크가 경로를 정한 곳입니다.

segments.src: Each scan there is a status message flowing back upstream, which is what refreshes the tracking page you check at breakfast.
segments.tr: 그곳에서 찍히는 스캔 하나하나는 상류로 흘러가는 상태 메시지이며, 이것이 아침 식사 때 확인하는 배송 추적 페이지를 갱신합니다.

segments.src: Two days later it's on your porch.
segments.tr: 이틀 뒤 소포가 현관 앞에 도착합니다.

segments.src: You saw six tracking updates.
segments.tr: 추적 업데이트는 여섯 번 보셨습니다.

segments.src: The systems exchanged roughly fifty messages, and any one of them going quiet is what turns "out for delivery" into a support ticket.
segments.tr: 그 사이 시스템들은 약 50개의 메시지를 주고받았고, 그중 하나라도 끊기면 "배송 출발"이 고객센터 문의로 바뀝니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Logistics runs on three cooperating systems: ERP (the order and the books), WMS (inside the warehouse), TMS (freight and carriers).
segments.tr: 1. 물류는 세 개의 시스템이 협력해 돌아갑니다. ERP(주문과 장부), WMS(창고 내부), TMS(화물과 운송사).

segments.src: 2. They talk through EDI transaction sets or APIs, and the integration seams — not the individual systems — are where most projects fail.
segments.tr: 2. 이 시스템들은 EDI 트랜잭션 세트나 API를 통해 소통하며, 대부분의 프로젝트가 실패하는 곳은 개별 시스템이 아니라 통합의 이음새입니다.

segments.src: 3. Barcodes and RFID are the data-capture layer; without accurate scans, every system downstream is confidently wrong.
segments.tr: 3. 바코드와 RFID는 데이터 수집 계층이며, 정확한 스캔이 없으면 그 아래의 모든 시스템은 자신 있게 틀립니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A distribution center needs to decide which bin to store an incoming pallet in, and which pick path a worker should walk.
segments.tr: **1.** 물류센터가 들어오는 파레트를 어느 빈에 보관할지, 그리고 작업자가 어떤 피킹 경로로 걸을지 결정해야 합니다.

segments.src: Which system handles this?
segments.tr: 어느 시스템이 이를 처리합니까?

segments.src: - A) ERP
segments.tr: - A) ERP

segments.src: - B) WMS
segments.tr: - B) WMS

segments.src: - C) TMS
segments.tr: - C) TMS

segments.src: - D) EDI
segments.tr: - D) EDI

segments.src: **2.** True or False: The main advantage of RFID over barcodes is that RFID tags are cheaper per unit.
segments.tr: **2.** 참/거짓: 바코드 대비 RFID의 주요 장점은 RFID 태그가 개당 더 저렴하다는 것이다.

segments.src: **3.** Your company is overpaying carriers because nobody checks freight invoices against contracted rates.
segments.tr: **3.** 회사가 운임 청구서를 계약 요율과 대조하지 않아 운송사에 과다 지불하고 있습니다.

segments.tr: 어떤 기능이 이 문제를 가장 직접적으로 해결합니까?

segments.src: - A) Cycle counting in the WMS
segments.tr: - A) WMS의 순환 재고 실사

segments.src: - B) Freight audit and pay in the TMS
segments.tr: - B) TMS의 운임 감사 및 지급

segments.src: - C) The item master in the ERP
segments.tr: - C) ERP의 품목 마스터

segments.src: - D) SSCC license plate labels
segments.tr: - D) SSCC 라이선스 플레이트 라벨

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** Software that directs work inside the warehouse — receiving, putaway, slotting, picking, packing, and cycle counting.
segments.tr: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** 창고 안의 작업을 지시하는 소프트웨어입니다. 입고, 적재, 슬로팅, 피킹, 포장, 순환 재고 실사를 담당합니다.

segments.src: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** Software that selects carriers and modes, consolidates and tenders loads, tracks freight, and audits carrier invoices.
segments.tr: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** 운송사와 운송 방식을 선택하고, 적재분을 묶어 입찰하며, 화물을 추적하고, 운송사 청구서를 감사하는 소프트웨어입니다.

segments.src: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** The company-wide system of record for orders, purchasing, item master data, and finance — the source WMS and TMS take direction from.
segments.tr: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** 주문, 구매, 품목 마스터 데이터, 재무를 위한 전사 차원의 기록 원천 시스템입니다. WMS와 TMS가 지시를 받는 출처입니다.

segments.src: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** Standardized business documents exchanged machine-to-machine (e.g., 856 advance ship notice, 214 shipment status), still the backbone of U.S. retail supply chains.
segments.tr: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** 기계 간에 교환되는 표준화된 비즈니스 문서입니다(예: 856 사전 출하 통지, 214 배송 상태). 여전히 미국 리테일 공급망의 근간입니다.

segments.src: - **SSCC / license plate:** An 18-digit serial number in a GS1-128 barcode on a pallet or carton, letting one scan retrieve everything that unit contains.
segments.tr: - **SSCC / 라이선스 플레이트:** 파레트나 카톤의 GS1-128 바코드에 담긴 18자리 일련번호로, 한 번의 스캔으로 그 단위에 담긴 모든 것을 불러올 수 있게 합니다.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** The WMS owns everything inside the four walls, including slotting and pick-path logic; the ERP holds the order, not the bin location.
segments.tr: *정답: **1 — B.** WMS는 슬로팅과 피킹 경로 로직을 포함해 창고 벽 안의 모든 것을 담당합니다. ERP는 주문을 보관할 뿐 빈 위치를 알지 못합니다.

segments.src: **2 — False.** RFID tags cost more than a printed barcode; the real advantage is bulk, no-line-of-sight reading — hundreds of tags at once, through packaging.
segments.tr: **2 — 거짓.** RFID 태그는 인쇄된 바코드보다 비쌉니다. 진짜 장점은 대량 판독과 시야 없이 읽기입니다. 포장을 통과해 한 번에 수백 개의 태그를 읽을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Freight audit and pay is a core TMS function, and recovering billing errors is often how a TMS pays for itself.*
segments.tr: **3 — B.** 운임 감사 및 지급은 TMS의 핵심 기능이며, 청구 오류를 회수하는 것이 종종 TMS가 비용을 회수하는 방식입니다.*

zh.title: [物流入门 101 #13] 你的包裹移动两次，它的数据移动五十次。

segments.src: > Warehouses and trucks move boxes, but software decides which box, which truck, and when — and that software is really three systems (WMS, TMS, ERP) stitched together by scans.
segments.tr: > 仓库和卡车负责移动箱子，但决定哪个箱子、哪辆卡车、何时移动的是软件——而这套软件实际上由三个系统（WMS、TMS、ERP）组成，并通过扫描串联在一起。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Picture the last thing you ordered online.
segments.tr: 想想你最近在网上下单的最后一件商品。

segments.src: Physically, it made maybe four moves: shelf to tote, tote to box, box to trailer, trailer to your porch.
segments.tr: 实际上，它大约经历了四次移动：从货架到周转箱，从周转箱到纸箱，从纸箱到拖车，再从拖车到你家门口。

segments.src: Digitally, it triggered dozens of transactions — an order record, an inventory allocation, a pick task, a carton label, a rate quote, a load tender, six or seven tracking scans, an invoice.
segments.tr: 而在数字层面，它触发了几十笔交易——一条订单记录、一次库存分配、一个拣货任务、一张箱标、一份运价报价、一次运输委托、六到七次物流追踪扫描，以及一张发票。

segments.src: That digital layer is the **logistics information system**, and in most companies it's not one product.
segments.tr: 这个数字层就是**物流信息系统**，而在大多数公司里，它并不是一个产品。

segments.src: It's three, each with its own job:
segments.tr: 它由三个系统组成，各自有不同的职责：

segments.src: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)** is the system of record — the company's books.
segments.tr: **ERP（企业资源计划）**是系统记录，即公司的账本。

segments.src: It holds the customer order, the purchase order, the item master, the price, the general ledger.
segments.tr: 它保存客户订单、采购订单、物料主数据、价格和总账。

segments.src: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.
segments.tr: SAP、Oracle、NetSuite、Microsoft Dynamics。

segments.src: The ERP knows *what* was promised to whom, but it has almost no idea where any physical carton is sitting right now.
segments.tr: ERP 知道*向谁承诺了什么*，但几乎不知道任何一个实物箱子此刻在哪里。

segments.src: **WMS (Warehouse Management System)** runs everything inside the four walls.
segments.tr: **WMS（仓库管理系统）**负责管理四面墙以内的所有作业。

segments.src: It directs receiving, decides where to putaway a pallet (slotting), generates pick tasks in an efficient walk path, controls packing and cartonization, manages cycle counts, and produces the shipping label.
segments.tr: 它指挥收货，决定托盘的上架位置（库位分配），生成高效行走路线的拣货任务，控制打包和装箱方式，管理循环盘点，并生成发运标签。

segments.src: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.
segments.tr: Manhattan Associates、Blue Yonder、Körber。

segments.src: The WMS is the only system that truly knows that SKU 44821 is in aisle 12, bin B, quantity 63.
segments.tr: WMS 是唯一真正知道 SKU 44821 位于 12 号通道 B 货位、数量为 63 的系统。

segments.src: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** takes over once freight leaves the dock — and often before.
segments.tr: **TMS（运输管理系统）**在货物离开月台后接手——有时甚至更早。

segments.src: It rates and compares carriers, picks the mode (parcel, LTL, truckload, intermodal), consolidates small orders into one load, tenders that load to a carrier, tracks it, and audits the freight bill against the contracted rate.
segments.tr: 它对承运商进行运价比较，选择运输方式（包裹、零担 LTL、整车 TL、多式联运），将小订单合并为一车，将该车货委托给承运商，跟踪运输过程，并将运费账单与合同运价进行核对。

segments.src: Overpaying carriers is shockingly common without one; freight audit alone often pays for the software.
segments.tr: 如果没有 TMS，多付运费的情况非常普遍；仅运费审计往往就能覆盖软件的成本。

segments.src: The hard part isn't any single system.
segments.tr: 真正的难点并不在于任何单一系统。

segments.src: It's **the seams**.
segments.tr: 而在于**衔接处**。

segments.src: In the U.S., those seams are usually crossed one of two ways: **EDI**, the decades-old transaction-set standard (a 940 tells the warehouse to ship, a 945 confirms it shipped, a 204 tenders a load to a trucker, a 214 sends status updates back, an 856 is the advance ship notice that tells the retailer what's on the truck), or modern **APIs**, which do the same thing in near real time.
segments.tr: 在美国，这些衔接处通常通过两种方式连接：**EDI**，即已有数十年历史的交易集标准（940 通知仓库发货，945 确认已发货，204 向承运人委托运输，214 回传状态更新，856 是预先发货通知，告诉零售商车上装了什么），或现代 **API**，二者以接近实时的方式完成同样的工作。

segments.src: A retail vendor who mis-formats an 856 gets a chargeback, not an email.
segments.tr: 如果零售供应商的 856 格式错误，得到的不是一封邮件，而是一张拒付通知。

segments.src: And all of it runs on one humble input: **the scan**.
segments.tr: 而所有这一切都依赖于一个朴素的输入：**扫描**。

segments.src: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)
segments.tr: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)

segments.src: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit
segments.tr: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit

segments.src: **Barcodes** are the workhorse.
segments.tr: **条码**是主力。

segments.src: A UPC identifies the product; a GS1-128 label on a pallet carries an SSCC — an 18-digit serial number that acts as a "license plate" so one scan pulls up the entire contents of that pallet.
segments.tr: UPC 用于标识商品；托盘上的 GS1-128 标签承载 SSCC——一个 18 位序列号，相当于“车牌”，一次扫描即可调出该托盘的全部内容。

segments.src: Barcodes are effectively free to print, but they need line of sight and one read at a time.
segments.tr: 条码的打印成本几乎为零，但需要视线可及，而且只能逐个读取。

segments.src: **RFID** (in retail supply chains, usually passive UHF "RAIN" RFID) flips that.
segments.tr: **RFID**（零售供应链中通常为无源超高频 “RAIN” RFID）则不同。

segments.src: A reader can pick up hundreds of tags at once, through a cardboard box, without anyone aiming anything.
segments.tr: 读取器可以同时读取数百个标签，即使隔着纸箱，也无需对准任何东西。

segments.src: Walk a handheld down a store aisle and count the inventory in minutes instead of hours.
segments.tr: 拿着手持设备走一遍卖场过道，几分钟就能完成库存盘点，而不是几个小时。

segments.src: The tradeoff is cost and physics: tags cost a few cents each at volume rather than nothing, and radio waves behave badly around metal and liquid.
segments.tr: 其代价在于成本和物理特性：大批量时标签每个只需几分钱，而不是免费；无线电波在金属和液体附近表现很差。

segments.src: That's why RFID took off first in apparel — light, non-metallic, high SKU count, and painful to count by hand — and why Walmart's expansion of its RFID tagging requirements beyond apparel starting in 2022 pushed a lot of suppliers into it.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么 RFID 最先在服装行业普及——服装轻、不含金属、SKU 数量庞大，而且手工盘点非常痛苦；也是为什么沃尔玛从 2022 年起将 RFID 标签要求扩展到服装以外的品类，促使大量供应商采用这项技术。

segments.src: The unglamorous truth: none of this fixes bad data.
segments.tr: 朴素的真相是：这些都无法修复糟糕的数据。

segments.src: If a receiver scans a pallet into the wrong bin, the WMS confidently tells a picker to walk to an empty shelf.
segments.tr: 如果收货员把托盘扫进了错误的货位，WMS 就会自信地指示拣货员走到一个空货架。

segments.src: Garbage in, expensive walk out.
segments.tr: 垃圾进，昂贵的白跑出。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: It's 11 p.m.
segments.tr: 晚上 11 点，

segments.src: in Columbus, Ohio, and you order a $110 pair of running shoes with free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: 在俄亥俄州哥伦布市，你下单了一双 110 美元的跑鞋，并享受免费两日达配送。

segments.src: The retailer's **ERP** captures the order and the payment.
segments.tr: 零售商的 **ERP** 记录订单和付款。

segments.src: Available-to-promise logic checks inventory and assigns it to a fulfillment center in Indiana rather than the one in Nevada — closer to you, cheaper to ship, and the shoes are actually there.
segments.tr: 可售量（ATP）逻辑核查库存，并将订单分配给印第安纳州的配送中心，而不是内华达州的那个——离你更近，运费更低，而且鞋子确实在那里。

segments.src: The **WMS** drops a pick task onto a handheld.
segments.tr: **WMS** 向手持终端下发一个拣货任务。

segments.src: A picker walks a route the system optimized, scans the shelf barcode (confirming the right location), scans the shoe box (confirming the right SKU), and drops it in a tote.
segments.tr: 拣货员沿着系统优化的路线行走，扫描货架条码（确认库位正确），扫描鞋盒（确认 SKU 正确），然后放入周转箱。

segments.src: Packing scans it again into a carton and prints a label.
segments.tr: 打包时再次扫描，装入纸箱，并打印标签。

segments.src: Every one of those scans is the system asking "prove it" — that's how inventory records stay honest.
segments.tr: 这些扫描中的每一次，都是系统在问“证明给我看”——正是这样，库存记录才能保持真实可靠。

segments.src: The **TMS** — or the parcel-rating engine that plays its role — compares carriers and service levels for that ZIP code, picks one, and transmits the shipment data before the box is even on the trailer.
segments.tr: **TMS**——或承担其角色的包裹运费计算引擎——会比较该邮编区域的承运商和服务等级，选定一家，并在箱子还未装上车之前就传输运单数据。

segments.src: That's why your tracking number goes live with "label created" while the box is still sitting in Indiana.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么你的追踪号码会显示“已创建运单”，而箱子此时仍在印第安纳州。

segments.src: Overnight the trailer runs to a sort hub — Memphis, Louisville, wherever the network routes it.
segments.tr: 夜间，车辆前往分拣中心——孟菲斯、路易斯维尔，或网络路由指定的任何地点。

segments.src: Each scan there is a status message flowing back upstream, which is what refreshes the tracking page you check at breakfast.
segments.tr: 在那里的每一次扫描，都会向上游回传一条状态消息，这正是刷新你早餐时查看的追踪页面的原因。

segments.src: Two days later it's on your porch.
segments.tr: 两天后，它出现在你家门口。

segments.src: You saw six tracking updates.
segments.tr: 你看到了六次追踪更新。

segments.src: The systems exchanged roughly fifty messages, and any one of them going quiet is what turns "out for delivery" into a support ticket.
segments.tr: 而系统之间交换了大约五十条消息，其中任何一条中断，都会让“派送中”变成一张客服工单。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三句话总结

segments.src: 1. Logistics runs on three cooperating systems: ERP (the order and the books), WMS (inside the warehouse), TMS (freight and carriers).
segments.tr: 1. 物流依靠三个协同工作的系统运行：ERP（订单与账务）、WMS（仓库内部）、TMS（货运与承运商）。

segments.src: 2. They talk through EDI transaction sets or APIs, and the integration seams — not the individual systems — are where most projects fail.
segments.tr: 2. 它们通过 EDI 交易集或 API 进行通信，而大多数项目的失败之处恰恰是集成衔接点，而非单个系统本身。

segments.src: 3. Barcodes and RFID are the data-capture layer; without accurate scans, every system downstream is confidently wrong.
segments.tr: 3. 条码和 RFID 是数据采集层；如果扫描数据不准确，下游的每个系统都会自信地得出错误结论。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **1.** A distribution center needs to decide which bin to store an incoming pallet in, and which pick path a worker should walk.
segments.tr: **1.** 配送中心需要决定将一个进货托盘存放在哪个货位，以及工人应走哪条拣货路线。

segments.src: Which system handles this?
segments.tr: 哪个系统负责此事？

segments.src: - A) ERP
segments.tr: - A) ERP

segments.src: - B) WMS
segments.tr: - B) WMS

segments.tr: - D) EDI

segments.tr: **2.** 判断对错：RFID 相对于条码的主要优势在于 RFID 标签单价更便宜。

segments.src: **3.** Your company is overpaying carriers because nobody checks freight invoices against contracted rates.
segments.tr: **3.** 你的公司因无人将货运账单与合同运价核对而多付了运费。

segments.src: Which capability addresses this most directly?
segments.tr: 哪项功能最直接地解决了这一问题？

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** Software that directs work inside the warehouse — receiving, putaway, slotting, picking, packing, and cycle counting.
segments.tr: - **WMS（仓库管理系统）：** 指挥仓库内作业的软件——收货、上架、库位分配、拣货、打包和循环盘点。

segments.src: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** Software that selects carriers and modes, consolidates and tenders loads, tracks freight, and audits carrier invoices.
segments.tr: - **TMS（运输管理系统）：** 负责选择承运商和运输方式、合并并委托运输、跟踪货物并审核承运商账单的软件。

segments.src: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** The company-wide system of record for orders, purchasing, item master data, and finance — the source WMS and TMS take direction from.
segments.tr: - **ERP（企业资源计划）：** 面向全公司的订单、采购、物料主数据和财务系统记录——WMS 和 TMS 的指令来源。

segments.src: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** Standardized business documents exchanged machine-to-machine (e.g., 856 advance ship notice, 214 shipment status), still the backbone of U.S. retail supply chains.
segments.tr: - **EDI（电子数据交换）：** 机器之间交换的标准化业务单据（例如 856 预先发货通知、214 运输状态），至今仍是美国零售供应链的骨干。

segments.src: - **SSCC / license plate:** An 18-digit serial number in a GS1-128 barcode on a pallet or carton, letting one scan retrieve everything that unit contains.
segments.tr: - **SSCC / 托盘标签：** 托盘或箱子上 GS1-128 条码中的 18 位序列号，使一次扫描即可获取该单元包含的全部内容。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** The WMS owns everything inside the four walls, including slotting and pick-path logic; the ERP holds the order, not the bin location.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — B.** WMS 负责四面墙以内的一切，包括库位分配和拣货路线逻辑；ERP 保存的是订单，而非货位位置。

segments.src: **2 — False.** RFID tags cost more than a printed barcode; the real advantage is bulk, no-line-of-sight reading — hundreds of tags at once, through packaging.
segments.tr: **2 — 错误。** RFID 标签的成本高于印刷条码；其真正优势在于批量读取、无需视线——可以穿透包装同时读取数百个标签。

segments.src: **3 — B.** Freight audit and pay is a core TMS function, and recovering billing errors is often how a TMS pays for itself.*
segments.tr: **3 — B.** 运费审计与付款是 TMS 的核心功能，而追回账单错误往往正是 TMS 收回成本的方式。*

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Picture the last thing you ordered online.
segments.tr: अपना आखिरी ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर याद कीजिए।

segments.src: Physically, it made maybe four moves: shelf to tote, tote to box, box to trailer, trailer to your porch.
segments.tr: भौतिक रूप से, उसने शायद चार चाल चली: शेल्फ़ से टोट, टोट से डिब्बा, डिब्बा से ट्रेलर, ट्रेलर से आपके दरवाज़े तक।

segments.src: Digitally, it triggered dozens of transactions — an order record, an inventory allocation, a pick task, a carton label, a rate quote, a load tender, six or seven tracking scans, an invoice.
segments.tr: डिजिटल रूप से, उसने दर्जनों लेन-देन शुरू किए: एक ऑर्डर रिकॉर्ड, इन्वेंटरी आवंटन, पिक टास्क, कार्टन लेबल, दर का अनुमान, लोड टेंडर, छह-सात ट्रैकिंग स्कैन, और एक इनवॉइस।

segments.src: That digital layer is the **logistics information system**, and in most companies it's not one product.
segments.tr: वह डिजिटल परत ही **लॉजिस्टिक्स सूचना प्रणाली** है, और ज़्यादातर कंपनियों में यह एक उत्पाद नहीं होती।

segments.src: It's three, each with its own job:
segments.tr: यह तीन होती है, और हर एक का अपना काम है:

segments.src: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)** is the system of record — the company's books.
segments.tr: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)** रिकॉर्ड की प्रणाली है, यानी कंपनी का बही-खाता।

segments.src: It holds the customer order, the purchase order, the item master, the price, the general ledger.
segments.tr: इसमें ग्राहक का ऑर्डर, खरीद ऑर्डर, आइटम मास्टर, कीमत और जनरल लेजर रहते हैं।

segments.src: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.
segments.tr: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.

segments.src: The ERP knows *what* was promised to whom, but it has almost no idea where any physical carton is sitting right now.
segments.tr: ERP को पता होता है कि *किससे क्या वादा किया गया था*, लेकिन उसे लगभग कोई अंदाज़ा नहीं होता कि कोई भौतिक कार्टन अभी कहाँ पड़ा है।

segments.src: **WMS (Warehouse Management System)** runs everything inside the four walls.
segments.tr: **WMS (Warehouse Management System)** चारदीवारी के भीतर सब कुछ चलाता है।

segments.src: It directs receiving, decides where to putaway a pallet (slotting), generates pick tasks in an efficient walk path, controls packing and cartonization, manages cycle counts, and produces the shipping label.
segments.tr: यह रिसीविंग का निर्देश देता है, तय करता है कि पैलेट कहाँ रखा जाए (slotting), कुशल रास्ते पर पिक टास्क बनाता है, पैकिंग और कार्टनाइज़ेशन नियंत्रित करता है, साइकिल काउंट संभालता है, और शिपिंग लेबल बनाता है।

segments.src: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.
segments.tr: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.

segments.src: The WMS is the only system that truly knows that SKU 44821 is in aisle 12, bin B, quantity 63.
segments.tr: WMS ही एकमात्र प्रणाली है जो सचमुच जानती है कि SKU 44821 गलियारा 12, बिन B में, मात्रा 63 में रखा है।

segments.src: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** takes over once freight leaves the dock — and often before.
segments.tr: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** तब शुरू होता है जब माल डॉक से निकलता है, और अक्सर उससे पहले भी।

segments.src: It rates and compares carriers, picks the mode (parcel, LTL, truckload, intermodal), consolidates small orders into one load, tenders that load to a carrier, tracks it, and audits the freight bill against the contracted rate.
segments.tr: यह कैरियर की दरों की तुलना करता है, मोड चुनता है (पार्सल, LTL, ट्रकलोड, इंटरमोडल), छोटे ऑर्डरों को एक लोड में समेकित करता है, वह लोड कैरियर को सौंपता है, उसे ट्रैक करता है, और फ़्रेट बिल का अनुबंधित दर से मिलान करता है।

segments.src: Overpaying carriers is shockingly common without one; freight audit alone often pays for the software.
segments.tr: TMS के बिना कैरियर को ज़्यादा भुगतान करना आश्चर्यजनक रूप से आम है; अकेला फ़्रेट ऑडिट अक्सर सॉफ़्टवेयर की लागत निकाल देता है।

segments.src: The hard part isn't any single system.
segments.tr: कठिन हिस्सा किसी एक सिस्टम का नहीं है।

segments.src: It's **the seams**.
segments.tr: यह **जोड़ (seams)** का है।

segments.src: In the U.S., those seams are usually crossed one of two ways: **EDI**, the decades-old transaction-set standard (a 940 tells the warehouse to ship, a 945 confirms it shipped, a 204 tenders a load to a trucker, a 214 sends status updates back, an 856 is the advance ship notice that tells the retailer what's on the truck), or modern **APIs**, which do the same thing in near real time.
segments.tr: अमेरिका में ये जोड़ आम तौर पर दो तरीकों से पार होते हैं: **EDI**, दशकों पुराना लेन-देन-सेट मानक (940 गोदाम को शिप करने का निर्देश देता है, 945 भेजे जाने की पुष्टि करता है, 204 ट्रकर को लोड टेंडर करता है, 214 स्थिति अपडेट वापस भेजता है, 856 एडवांस शिप नोटिस है जो रिटेलर को बताता है कि ट्रक में क्या है), या आधुनिक **API**, जो लगभग वास्तविक समय में यही काम करते हैं।

segments.src: A retail vendor who mis-formats an 856 gets a chargeback, not an email.
segments.tr: कोई रिटेल विक्रेता अगर 856 गलत प्रारूप में भेजता है, तो उसे ईमेल नहीं, चार्जबैक मिलता है।

segments.src: And all of it runs on one humble input: **the scan**.
segments.tr: और यह सब एक साधारण इनपुट पर चलता है: **स्कैन**।

segments.src: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)
segments.tr: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)

segments.src: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit
segments.tr: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit

segments.src: **Barcodes** are the workhorse.
segments.tr: **बारकोड** मुख्य काम करने वाले हैं।

segments.src: A UPC identifies the product; a GS1-128 label on a pallet carries an SSCC — an 18-digit serial number that acts as a "license plate" so one scan pulls up the entire contents of that pallet.
segments.tr: UPC उत्पाद की पहचान करता है; पैलेट पर लगा GS1-128 लेबल एक SSCC रखता है, यानी 18-अंकीय सीरियल नंबर जो "लाइसेंस प्लेट" की तरह काम करता है, ताकि एक स्कैन से उस पैलेट की पूरी सामग्री सामने आ जाए।

segments.src: Barcodes are effectively free to print, but they need line of sight and one read at a time.
segments.tr: बारकोड छापने में लगभग मुफ़्त हैं, लेकिन उन्हें सीधी दृष्टि-रेखा और एक बार में एक ही पढ़ाई चाहिए।

segments.src: **RFID** (in retail supply chains, usually passive UHF "RAIN" RFID) flips that.
segments.tr: **RFID** (रिटेल सप्लाई चेन में आम तौर पर पैसिव UHF "RAIN" RFID) इसे उलट देता है।

segments.src: A reader can pick up hundreds of tags at once, through a cardboard box, without anyone aiming anything.
segments.tr: एक रीडर बिना किसी को निशाना लगाए, गत्ते के डिब्बे के आर-पार, एक साथ सैकड़ों टैग पढ़ सकता है।

segments.src: Walk a handheld down a store aisle and count the inventory in minutes instead of hours.
segments.tr: हैंडहेल्ड लेकर स्टोर के गलियारे में चलिए और घंटों के बजाय मिनटों में इन्वेंटरी गिन लीजिए।

segments.src: The tradeoff is cost and physics: tags cost a few cents each at volume rather than nothing, and radio waves behave badly around metal and liquid.
segments.tr: समझौता लागत और भौतिकी का है: बड़ी मात्रा में टैग की कीमत प्रति टैग कुछ पैसे होती है, जबकि बारकोड लगभग मुफ़्त है, और रेडियो तरंगें धातु और तरल के आसपास ठीक से काम नहीं करतीं।

segments.src: That's why RFID took off first in apparel — light, non-metallic, high SKU count, and painful to count by hand — and why Walmart's expansion of its RFID tagging requirements beyond apparel starting in 2022 pushed a lot of suppliers into it.
segments.tr: इसीलिए RFID पहले अपैरल में चला: हल्का, अधातु, अधिक SKU संख्या, और हाथ से गिनना कष्टदायक। और 2022 से Walmart द्वारा अपैरल से आगे RFID टैगिंग आवश्यकताओं का विस्तार करने से कई आपूर्तिकर्ता इसे अपनाने को मजबूर हुए।

segments.src: The unglamorous truth: none of this fixes bad data.
segments.tr: सीधी सच्चाई यह है: इनमें से कुछ भी खराब डेटा को ठीक नहीं करता।

segments.src: If a receiver scans a pallet into the wrong bin, the WMS confidently tells a picker to walk to an empty shelf.
segments.tr: अगर कोई रिसीवर पैलेट को गलत बिन में स्कैन करता है, तो WMS आत्मविश्वास से पिकर को एक खाली शेल्फ़ की ओर भेज देता है।

segments.src: Garbage in, expensive walk out.
segments.tr: गलत इनपुट, महँगा चक्कर।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा के जीवन में

segments.src: It's 11 p.m.
segments.tr: रात के 11 बजे

segments.src: in Columbus, Ohio, and you order a $110 pair of running shoes with free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: ओहायो के कोलंबस में, और आप $110 के रनिंग शूज़ का ऑर्डर देते हैं जिस पर मुफ़्त दो-दिवसीय शिपिंग है।

segments.src: The retailer's **ERP** captures the order and the payment.
segments.tr: रिटेलर का **ERP** ऑर्डर और भुगतान दर्ज करता है।

segments.src: Available-to-promise logic checks inventory and assigns it to a fulfillment center in Indiana rather than the one in Nevada — closer to you, cheaper to ship, and the shoes are actually there.
segments.tr: Available-to-promise लॉजिक इन्वेंटरी जाँचता है और उसे नेवाडा के बजाय इंडियाना के फ़ुलफ़िलमेंट सेंटर को सौंपता है। वह आपके पास है, शिपिंग में सस्ता है, और जूते सचमुच वहीं हैं।

segments.src: The **WMS** drops a pick task onto a handheld.
segments.tr: **WMS** एक हैंडहेल्ड पर पिक टास्क भेजता है।

segments.src: A picker walks a route the system optimized, scans the shelf barcode (confirming the right location), scans the shoe box (confirming the right SKU), and drops it in a tote.
segments.tr: एक पिकर सिस्टम के अनुकूलित रास्ते पर चलता है, शेल्फ़ का बारकोड स्कैन करता है (सही स्थान की पुष्टि), जूते के डिब्बे को स्कैन करता है (सही SKU की पुष्टि), और उसे टोट में डाल देता है।

segments.src: Packing scans it again into a carton and prints a label.
segments.tr: पैकिंग उसे फिर से स्कैन करके एक कार्टन में डालती है और लेबल छापती है।

segments.src: Every one of those scans is the system asking "prove it" — that's how inventory records stay honest.
segments.tr: इन सभी स्कैनों में से हर एक सिस्टम का यह पूछना है "साबित करो"। इसी से इन्वेंटरी रिकॉर्ड ईमानदार रहते हैं।

segments.src: The **TMS** — or the parcel-rating engine that plays its role — compares carriers and service levels for that ZIP code, picks one, and transmits the shipment data before the box is even on the trailer.
segments.tr: **TMS**, या उसकी भूमिका निभाने वाला पार्सल-रेटिंग इंजन, उस ZIP कोड के लिए कैरियर और सेवा स्तर की तुलना करता है, एक चुनता है, और बॉक्स ट्रेलर पर चढ़ने से पहले ही शिपमेंट डेटा भेज देता है।

segments.src: That's why your tracking number goes live with "label created" while the box is still sitting in Indiana.
segments.tr: इसीलिए आपका ट्रैकिंग नंबर "लेबल बनाया गया" के साथ सक्रिय हो जाता है, जबकि बॉक्स अभी इंडियाना में ही पड़ा होता है।

segments.src: Overnight the trailer runs to a sort hub — Memphis, Louisville, wherever the network routes it.
segments.tr: रात भर ट्रेलर एक सॉर्ट हब की ओर चलता है: मेम्फ़िस, लुइसविल, या जहाँ भी नेटवर्क उसे भेजे।

segments.src: Each scan there is a status message flowing back upstream, which is what refreshes the tracking page you check at breakfast.
segments.tr: वहाँ हर स्कैन एक स्थिति संदेश है जो ऊपर की ओर बहता है, और यही नाश्ते के समय आपके द्वारा देखे जा रहे ट्रैकिंग पेज को ताज़ा करता है।

segments.src: Two days later it's on your porch.
segments.tr: दो दिन बाद वह आपके दरवाज़े पर होता है।

segments.src: You saw six tracking updates.
segments.tr: आपने छह ट्रैकिंग अपडेट देखे।

segments.src: The systems exchanged roughly fifty messages, and any one of them going quiet is what turns "out for delivery" into a support ticket.
segments.tr: सिस्टमों ने लगभग पचास संदेशों का आदान-प्रदान किया, और उनमें से किसी एक का चुप हो जाना ही "डिलीवरी के लिए निकला" को सपोर्ट टिकट में बदल देता है।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Logistics runs on three cooperating systems: ERP (the order and the books), WMS (inside the warehouse), TMS (freight and carriers).
segments.tr: 1. लॉजिस्टिक्स तीन सहयोगी सिस्टमों पर चलता है: ERP (ऑर्डर और बही-खाता), WMS (गोदाम के भीतर), TMS (माल और कैरियर)।

segments.src: 2. They talk through EDI transaction sets or APIs, and the integration seams — not the individual systems — are where most projects fail.
segments.tr: 2. वे EDI लेन-देन-सेट या API के ज़रिए बात करते हैं, और एकीकरण के जोड़, न कि अलग-अलग सिस्टम, वही जगह हैं जहाँ ज़्यादातर परियोजनाएँ विफल होती हैं।

segments.src: 3. Barcodes and RFID are the data-capture layer; without accurate scans, every system downstream is confidently wrong.
segments.tr: 3. बारकोड और RFID डेटा-कैप्चर परत हैं; सटीक स्कैन के बिना, आगे का हर सिस्टम आत्मविश्वास से गलत होता है।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** Software that directs work inside the warehouse — receiving, putaway, slotting, picking, packing, and cycle counting.
segments.tr: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** गोदाम के भीतर काम का निर्देश देने वाला सॉफ़्टवेयर: रिसीविंग, पुटअवे, slotting, पिकिंग, पैकिंग और साइकिल काउंटिंग।

segments.src: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** Software that selects carriers and modes, consolidates and tenders loads, tracks freight, and audits carrier invoices.
segments.tr: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** सॉफ़्टवेयर जो कैरियर और मोड चुनता है, लोड समेकित करता और टेंडर करता है, माल को ट्रैक करता है, और कैरियर इनवॉइस का ऑडिट करता है।

segments.src: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** The company-wide system of record for orders, purchasing, item master data, and finance — the source WMS and TMS take direction from.
segments.tr: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** ऑर्डर, खरीद, आइटम मास्टर डेटा और वित्त के लिए कंपनी-व्यापी रिकॉर्ड की प्रणाली, यानी वह स्रोत जिससे WMS और TMS निर्देश लेते हैं।

segments.src: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** Standardized business documents exchanged machine-to-machine (e.g., 856 advance ship notice, 214 shipment status), still the backbone of U.S. retail supply chains.

es.title: [Logística 101 #13] Tu paquete se mueve dos veces. Sus datos se mueven cincuenta veces.

segments.src: > Warehouses and trucks move boxes, but software decides which box, which truck, and when — and that software is really three systems (WMS, TMS, ERP) stitched together by scans.
segments.tr: > Los almacenes y los camiones mueven cajas, pero es el software el que decide qué caja, qué camión y cuándo, y ese software son en realidad tres sistemas (WMS, TMS, ERP) unidos mediante escaneos.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Picture the last thing you ordered online.
segments.tr: Piensa en lo último que compraste en línea.

segments.src: Physically, it made maybe four moves: shelf to tote, tote to box, box to trailer, trailer to your porch.
segments.tr: Físicamente, hizo quizá cuatro movimientos: de la estantería al contenedor, del contenedor a la caja, de la caja al remolque y del remolque a tu porche.

segments.src: Digitally, it triggered dozens of transactions — an order record, an inventory allocation, a pick task, a carton label, a rate quote, a load tender, six or seven tracking scans, an invoice.
segments.tr: Digitalmente, activó decenas de transacciones: un registro del pedido, una asignación de inventario, una tarea de picking, una etiqueta de cartón, una cotización de tarifa, una oferta de carga, seis o siete escaneos de seguimiento y una factura.

segments.src: That digital layer is the **logistics information system**, and in most companies it's not one product.
segments.tr: Esa capa digital es el **sistema de información logística**, y en la mayoría de las empresas no es un solo producto.

segments.src: It's three, each with its own job:
segments.tr: Son tres, cada uno con su función:

segments.src: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)** is the system of record — the company's books.
segments.tr: **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning, planificación de recursos empresariales)** es el sistema de registro, los libros de la empresa.

segments.src: It holds the customer order, the purchase order, the item master, the price, the general ledger.
segments.tr: Guarda el pedido del cliente, la orden de compra, el maestro de artículos, el precio y el libro mayor.

segments.src: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.
segments.tr: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics.

segments.src: The ERP knows *what* was promised to whom, but it has almost no idea where any physical carton is sitting right now.
segments.tr: El ERP sabe *qué* se prometió a quién, pero casi no sabe dónde está en este momento ninguna caja física.

segments.src: **WMS (Warehouse Management System)** runs everything inside the four walls.
segments.tr: **WMS (Warehouse Management System, sistema de gestión de almacenes)** gestiona todo dentro de las cuatro paredes.

segments.src: It directs receiving, decides where to putaway a pallet (slotting), generates pick tasks in an efficient walk path, controls packing and cartonization, manages cycle counts, and produces the shipping label.
segments.tr: Dirige la recepción, decide dónde ubicar un palé al almacenarlo (slotting), genera tareas de picking con una ruta de recorrido eficiente, controla el embalaje y la encartonación, gestiona los inventarios cíclicos y genera la etiqueta de envío.

segments.src: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.
segments.tr: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.

segments.src: The WMS is the only system that truly knows that SKU 44821 is in aisle 12, bin B, quantity 63.
segments.tr: El WMS es el único sistema que realmente sabe que el SKU 44821 está en el pasillo 12, ubicación B, cantidad 63.

segments.src: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** takes over once freight leaves the dock — and often before.
segments.tr: **TMS (Transportation Management System, sistema de gestión del transporte)** toma el control en cuanto la mercancía sale del muelle, y a menudo incluso antes.

segments.src: It rates and compares carriers, picks the mode (parcel, LTL, truckload, intermodal), consolidates small orders into one load, tenders that load to a carrier, tracks it, and audits the freight bill against the contracted rate.
segments.tr: Tarifa y compara transportistas, elige el modo (paquetería, LTL, camión completo, intermodal), consolida pedidos pequeños en una sola carga, ofrece esa carga a un transportista, la rastrea y audita la factura de flete frente a la tarifa contratada.

segments.src: Overpaying carriers is shockingly common without one; freight audit alone often pays for the software.
segments.tr: Pagar de más a los transportistas es sorprendentemente común sin uno; solo la auditoría de fletes a menudo paga el software.

segments.src: The hard part isn't any single system.
segments.tr: La parte difícil no es ningún sistema por separado.

segments.src: It's **the seams**.
segments.tr: Son **las uniones**.

segments.src: In the U.S., those seams are usually crossed one of two ways: **EDI**, the decades-old transaction-set standard (a 940 tells the warehouse to ship, a 945 confirms it shipped, a 204 tenders a load to a trucker, a 214 sends status updates back, an 856 is the advance ship notice that tells the retailer what's on the truck), or modern **APIs**, which do the same thing in near real time.
segments.tr: En Estados Unidos, esas uniones suelen cruzarse de dos maneras: **EDI**, el estándar de conjuntos de transacciones de décadas de antigüedad (un 940 indica al almacén que envíe, un 945 confirma el envío, un 204 ofrece una carga a un transportista, un 214 devuelve las actualizaciones de estado, y un 856 es el aviso de envío anticipado que le dice al minorista qué lleva el camión), o las **API** modernas, que hacen lo mismo casi en tiempo real.

segments.src: A retail vendor who mis-formats an 856 gets a chargeback, not an email.
segments.tr: Un proveedor minorista que formatea mal un 856 recibe un cargo por devolución, no un correo electrónico.

segments.src: And all of it runs on one humble input: **the scan**.
segments.tr: Y todo ello funciona con una entrada muy humilde: **el escaneo**.

segments.src: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)
segments.tr: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)

segments.src: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit
segments.tr: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit

segments.src: **Barcodes** are the workhorse.
segments.tr: Los **códigos de barras** son el caballo de batalla.

segments.src: A UPC identifies the product; a GS1-128 label on a pallet carries an SSCC — an 18-digit serial number that acts as a "license plate" so one scan pulls up the entire contents of that pallet.
segments.tr: Un UPC identifica el producto; una etiqueta GS1-128 en un palé lleva un SSCC, un número de serie de 18 dígitos que actúa como "matrícula" para que un solo escaneo muestre todo el contenido de ese palé.

segments.src: Barcodes are effectively free to print, but they need line of sight and one read at a time.
segments.tr: Los códigos de barras prácticamente no cuestan nada imprimirlos, pero necesitan línea de visión y se leen uno a uno.

segments.src: **RFID** (in retail supply chains, usually passive UHF "RAIN" RFID) flips that.
segments.tr: El **RFID** (en las cadenas de suministro minoristas, normalmente RFID UHF pasivo "RAIN") cambia eso.

segments.src: A reader can pick up hundreds of tags at once, through a cardboard box, without anyone aiming anything.
segments.tr: Un lector puede captar cientos de etiquetas a la vez, a través de una caja de cartón, sin que nadie tenga que apuntar a nada.

segments.src: Walk a handheld down a store aisle and count the inventory in minutes instead of hours.
segments.tr: Pasa un lector portátil por un pasillo de la tienda y cuenta el inventario en minutos en lugar de horas.

segments.src: The tradeoff is cost and physics: tags cost a few cents each at volume rather than nothing, and radio waves behave badly around metal and liquid.
segments.tr: La contrapartida son el coste y la física: las etiquetas cuestan unos céntimos cada una en volumen, en lugar de nada, y las ondas de radio se comportan mal cerca de metal y líquidos.

segments.src: That's why RFID took off first in apparel — light, non-metallic, high SKU count, and painful to count by hand — and why Walmart's expansion of its RFID tagging requirements beyond apparel starting in 2022 pushed a lot of suppliers into it.
segments.tr: Por eso el RFID se impuso primero en la confección: es ligero, no metálico, tiene un número muy alto de SKU y contarlo a mano es un suplicio. Y por eso la ampliación de los requisitos de etiquetado RFID de Walmart más allá de la confección, a partir de 2022, empujó a muchos proveedores a adoptarlo.

segments.src: The unglamorous truth: none of this fixes bad data.
segments.tr: La verdad poco vistosa es que nada de esto arregla los datos malos.

segments.src: If a receiver scans a pallet into the wrong bin, the WMS confidently tells a picker to walk to an empty shelf.
segments.tr: Si un receptor escanea un palé en la ubicación equivocada, el WMS indica con total seguridad a un preparador que camine hasta una estantería vacía.

segments.src: Garbage in, expensive walk out.
segments.tr: Entrada basura, recorrido caro.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: It's 11 p.m.
segments.tr: Son las 23:00

segments.src: in Columbus, Ohio, and you order a $110 pair of running shoes with free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: en Columbus, Ohio, y pides un par de zapatillas para correr de 110 $ con envío gratuito en dos días.

segments.src: The retailer's **ERP** captures the order and the payment.
segments.tr: El **ERP** del minorista registra el pedido y el pago.

segments.src: Available-to-promise logic checks inventory and assigns it to a fulfillment center in Indiana rather than the one in Nevada — closer to you, cheaper to ship, and the shoes are actually there.
segments.tr: La lógica de disponibilidad para la venta (available-to-promise) comprueba el inventario y asigna el pedido a un centro de distribución en Indiana en lugar de al de Nevada: más cerca de ti, más barato de enviar y los zapatos están allí.

segments.src: The **WMS** drops a pick task onto a handheld.
segments.tr: El **WMS** envía una tarea de picking a un terminal portátil.

segments.src: A picker walks a route the system optimized, scans the shelf barcode (confirming the right location), scans the shoe box (confirming the right SKU), and drops it in a tote.
segments.tr: Un preparador recorre una ruta optimizada por el sistema, escanea la etiqueta de la estantería (confirmando la ubicación correcta), escanea la caja de los zapatos (confirmando el SKU correcto) y la deposita en un contenedor.

segments.src: Packing scans it again into a carton and prints a label.
segments.tr: El embalaje la escanea de nuevo, la mete en un cartón e imprime una etiqueta.

segments.src: Every one of those scans is the system asking "prove it" — that's how inventory records stay honest.
segments.tr: Cada uno de esos escaneos es el sistema preguntando «demuéstralo»: así es como los registros de inventario se mantienen fiables.

segments.src: The **TMS** — or the parcel-rating engine that plays its role — compares carriers and service levels for that ZIP code, picks one, and transmits the shipment data before the box is even on the trailer.
segments.tr: El **TMS** (o el motor de tarifas de paquetería que cumple ese papel) compara transportistas y niveles de servicio para ese código postal, elige uno y transmite los datos del envío antes de que la caja esté siquiera en el remolque.

segments.src: That's why your tracking number goes live with "label created" while the box is still sitting in Indiana.
segments.tr: Por eso tu número de seguimiento se activa con "etiqueta creada" mientras la caja sigue en Indiana.

segments.src: Overnight the trailer runs to a sort hub — Memphis, Louisville, wherever the network routes it.
segments.tr: Durante la noche, el remolque se dirige a un centro de clasificación: Memphis, Louisville o donde la red lo enrute.

segments.src: Each scan there is a status message flowing back upstream, which is what refreshes the tracking page you check at breakfast.
segments.tr: Cada escaneo allí es un mensaje de estado que vuelve aguas arriba, y eso es lo que actualiza la página de seguimiento que consultas en el desayuno.

segments.src: Two days later it's on your porch.
segments.tr: Dos días después, llega a tu porche.

segments.src: You saw six tracking updates.
segments.tr: Viste seis actualizaciones de seguimiento.

segments.src: The systems exchanged roughly fifty messages, and any one of them going quiet is what turns "out for delivery" into a support ticket.
segments.tr: Los sistemas intercambiaron unos cincuenta mensajes, y basta con que cualquiera de ellos se quede callado para que "en reparto" se convierta en un ticket de soporte.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen en tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Logistics runs on three cooperating systems: ERP (the order and the books), WMS (inside the warehouse), TMS (freight and carriers).
segments.tr: 1. La logística funciona con tres sistemas que cooperan: ERP (el pedido y los libros), WMS (dentro del almacén) y TMS (fletes y transportistas).

segments.src: 2. They talk through EDI transaction sets or APIs, and the integration seams — not the individual systems — are where most projects fail.
segments.tr: 2. Se comunican mediante conjuntos de transacciones EDI o API, y las uniones de integración (no los sistemas individuales) son donde fracasan la mayoría de los proyectos.

segments.src: 3. Barcodes and RFID are the data-capture layer; without accurate scans, every system downstream is confidently wrong.
segments.tr: 3. Los códigos de barras y el RFID son la capa de captura de datos; sin escaneos precisos, cada sistema posterior se equivoca con total seguridad.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.tr: **1.** Un centro de distribución necesita decidir en qué ubicación almacenar un palé entrante y por qué ruta de picking debe caminar un trabajador.

segments.tr: ¿Qué sistema se encarga de esto?

segments.tr: **2.** Verdadero o falso: la principal ventaja del RFID frente a los códigos de barras es que las etiquetas RFID son más baratas por unidad.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** Software that directs work inside the warehouse — receiving, putaway, slotting, picking, packing, and cycle counting.
segments.tr: - **WMS (Warehouse Management System):** Software que dirige el trabajo dentro del almacén: recepción, almacenamiento, asignación de ubicaciones (slotting), picking, embalaje e inventarios cíclicos.

segments.src: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** Software that selects carriers and modes, consolidates and tenders loads, tracks freight, and audits carrier invoices.
segments.tr: - **TMS (Transportation Management System):** Software que selecciona transportistas y modos, consolida y ofrece cargas, rastrea el flete y audita las facturas de los transportistas.

segments.src: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** The company-wide system of record for orders, purchasing, item master data, and finance — the source WMS and TMS take direction from.
segments.tr: - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** El sistema de registro de toda la empresa para pedidos, compras, datos maestros de artículos y finanzas: la fuente de la que el WMS y el TMS reciben instrucciones.

segments.src: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** Standardized business documents exchanged machine-to-machine (e.g., 856 advance ship notice, 214 shipment status), still the backbone of U.S. retail supply chains.
segments.tr: - **EDI (Electronic Data Interchange):** Documentos comerciales estandarizados que se intercambian de máquina a máquina (p. ej., 856 aviso de envío anticipado, 214 estado del envío), que siguen siendo la columna vertebral de las cadenas de suministro minoristas de EE. UU.

segments.src: - **SSCC / license plate:** An 18-digit serial number in a GS1-128 barcode on a pallet or carton, letting one scan retrieve everything that unit contains.
segments.tr: - **SSCC / matrícula:** Un número de serie de 18 dígitos en un código de barras GS1-128 de un palé o cartón, que permite que un solo escaneo recupere todo lo que contiene esa unidad.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** The WMS owns everything inside the four walls, including slotting and pick-path logic; the ERP holds the order, not the bin location.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — B.** El WMS controla todo lo que hay dentro de las cuatro paredes, incluida la asignación de ubicaciones (slotting) y la lógica de ruta de picking; el ERP guarda el pedido, no la ubicación en la estantería.

segments.src: **2 — False.** RFID tags cost more than a printed barcode; the real advantage is bulk, no-line-of-sight reading — hundreds of tags at once, through packaging.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** Las etiquetas RFID cuestan más que un código de barras impreso; la verdadera ventaja es la lectura masiva sin línea de visión: cientos de etiquetas a la vez, a través del embalaje.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Freight audit and pay is a core TMS function, and recovering billing errors is often how a TMS pays for itself.*
segments.tr: **3 — B.** La auditoría y el pago de fletes es una función central del TMS, y recuperar errores de facturación es a menudo la forma en que un TMS se paga a sí mismo.*

segments.tr: **WMS (نظام إدارة المستودعات)** يدير كل شيء داخل جدران المستودع الأربعة.

segments.src: It directs receiving, decides where to putaway a pallet (slotting), generates pick tasks in an efficient walk path, controls packing and cartonization, manages cycle counts, and produces the shipping label.
segments.tr: يوجّه عمليات الاستلام، ويقرر أين يُوضع البالت عند التخزين (slotting)، وينشئ مهام الالتقاط وفق مسار مشي فعّال، ويتحكم في التعبئة وتكوين الكراتين، ويدير جرد الدورات، ويُنتج ملصق الشحن.

segments.src: Manhattan Associates, Blue Yonder, Körber.
segments.tr: Manhattan Associates وBlue Yonder وKörber.

segments.src: The WMS is the only system that truly knows that SKU 44821 is in aisle 12, bin B, quantity 63.
segments.tr: نظام WMS هو النظام الوحيد الذي يعرف فعلاً أن الوحدة SKU 44821 موجودة في الممر 12، والصندوق B، وبكمية 63.

segments.src: **TMS (Transportation Management System)** takes over once freight leaves the dock — and often before.
segments.tr: **TMS (نظام إدارة النقل)** يتولى المهمة بمجرد خروج الشحنة من رصيف التحميل — وغالباً قبل ذلك.

segments.src: It rates and compares carriers, picks the mode (parcel, LTL, truckload, intermodal), consolidates small orders into one load, tenders that load to a carrier, tracks it, and audits the freight bill against the contracted rate.
segments.tr: يقيّم الناقلين ويقارن بينهم، ويختار وسيلة النقل (طرود، أو LTL، أو شاحنة كاملة، أو متعددة الوسائط)، ويجمع الطلبات الصغيرة في حمولة واحدة، ويعرض هذه الحمولة على الناقل، ويتتبعها، ويدقق فاتورة الشحن مقابل السعر المتعاقد عليه.

segments.src: Overpaying carriers is shockingly common without one; freight audit alone often pays for the software.
segments.tr: دفع مبالغ زائدة للناقلين شائع بشكل مدهش دون هذا النظام؛ إذ إن تدقيق الشحن وحده غالباً ما يغطي تكلفة البرنامج.

segments.src: The hard part isn't any single system.
segments.tr: الجزء الصعب ليس في أي نظام بمفرده.

segments.src: It's **the seams**.
segments.tr: بل في **نقاط الربط بينها**.

segments.src: In the U.S., those seams are usually crossed one of two ways: **EDI**, the decades-old transaction-set standard (a 940 tells the warehouse to ship, a 945 confirms it shipped, a 204 tenders a load to a trucker, a 214 sends status updates back, an 856 is the advance ship notice that tells the retailer what's on the truck), or modern **APIs**, which do the same thing in near real time.
segments.tr: في الولايات المتحدة، تُعبر هذه النقاط عادةً بإحدى طريقتين: **EDI**، وهو معيار مجموعات المعاملات القديم الذي يعود لعقود (فالرسالة 940 تأمر المستودع بالشحن، والرسالة 945 تؤكد أنه تم الشحن، والرسالة 204 تعرض حمولة على ناقل بري، والرسالة 214 ترسل تحديثات الحالة مرة أخرى، والرسالة 856 هي إشعار الشحن المسبق الذي يخبر تاجر التجزئة بما في الشاحنة)، أو **واجهات APIs** الحديثة، التي تقوم بالمهمة نفسها تقريباً في الوقت الفعلي.

segments.src: A retail vendor who mis-formats an 856 gets a chargeback, not an email.
segments.tr: أي بائع تجزئة يُخطئ في تنسيق الرسالة 856 يتلقى خصماً مالياً (chargeback)، لا مجرد بريد إلكتروني.

segments.src: And all of it runs on one humble input: **the scan**.
segments.tr: وكل ذلك يعتمد على مدخل بسيط واحد: **عملية المسح الضوئي**.

segments.src: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)
segments.tr: Order (ERP) -> allocate -> pick & pack (WMS) -> label -> tender (TMS)

segments.src: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit
segments.tr: -> carrier scans -> status back to ERP -> invoice -> freight audit

segments.src: **Barcodes** are the workhorse.
segments.tr: **الباركود** هو حصان العمل الأساسي.

segments.src: A UPC identifies the product; a GS1-128 label on a pallet carries an SSCC — an 18-digit serial number that acts as a "license plate" so one scan pulls up the entire contents of that pallet.
segments.tr: يُعرّف رمز UPC المنتج؛ وملصق GS1-128 على البالت يحمل رقم SSCC — وهو رقم تسلسلي من 18 خانة يعمل كـ"لوحة ترخيص" بحيث يعرض مسح واحد محتويات البالت بأكملها.

segments.src: Barcodes are effectively free to print, but they need line of sight and one read at a time.
segments.tr: الباركود مجاني عملياً للطباعة، لكنه يحتاج إلى خط رؤية واضح وقراءة واحدة في كل مرة.

segments.src: **RFID** (in retail supply chains, usually passive UHF "RAIN" RFID) flips that.
segments.tr: **RFID** (في سلاسل التوريد للتجزئة، عادةً RFID سلبي من نوع UHF، المعروف بـ"RAIN") يقلب هذا الوضع.

segments.src: A reader can pick up hundreds of tags at once, through a cardboard box, without anyone aiming anything.
segments.tr: يمكن للقارئ التقاط مئات العلامات دفعة واحدة، من خلال صندوق من الكرتون، دون الحاجة إلى توجيه أي شيء.

segments.src: Walk a handheld down a store aisle and count the inventory in minutes instead of hours.
segments.tr: امشِ بجهاز محمول في ممر متجر وأحصِ المخزون خلال دقائق بدلاً من ساعات.

segments.src: The tradeoff is cost and physics: tags cost a few cents each at volume rather than nothing, and radio waves behave badly around metal and liquid.
segments.tr: المقايضة تتعلق بالتكلفة والفيزياء: تكلّف العلامات بضعة سنتات لكل واحدة بالكميات الكبيرة بدلاً من لا شيء، والموجات الراديوية تتصرف بشكل سيئ بالقرب من المعادن والسوائل.

segments.src: That's why RFID took off first in apparel — light, non-metallic, high SKU count, and painful to count by hand — and why Walmart's expansion of its RFID tagging requirements beyond apparel starting in 2022 pushed a lot of suppliers into it.
segments.tr: ولهذا انتشرت تقنية RFID أولاً في الملابس — فهي خفيفة، وغير معدنية، ولها عدد كبير من الـSKU، ومرهقة للعد يدوياً — ولهذا أدى توسع متجر Walmart في متطلبات وسم RFID إلى ما هو أبعد من الملابس بدءاً من عام 2022 إلى دفع الكثير من الموردين نحوها.

segments.src: The unglamorous truth: none of this fixes bad data.
segments.tr: الحقيقة غير البراقة: لا شيء من هذا يُصلح البيانات السيئة.

segments.src: If a receiver scans a pallet into the wrong bin, the WMS confidently tells a picker to walk to an empty shelf.
segments.tr: إذا قام مستلم بمسح بالت ووضعه في الصندوق الخطأ، فسيوجّه نظام WMS الملتقط بثقة إلى رف فارغ.

segments.src: Garbage in, expensive walk out.
segments.tr: مدخلات سيئة، ومشي مكلف.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: It's 11 p.m.
segments.tr: الساعة 11 مساءً

segments.src: in Columbus, Ohio, and you order a $110 pair of running shoes with free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: في كولومبوس بولاية أوهايو، وتطلب زوجاً من أحذية الجري بسعر 110 دولارات مع شحن مجاني خلال يومين.

segments.src: The retailer's **ERP** captures the order and the payment.
segments.tr: يسجّل **ERP** الخاص بالمتجر الطلب والدفع.

segments.src: Available-to-promise logic checks inventory and assigns it to a fulfillment center in Indiana rather than the one in Nevada — closer to you, cheaper to ship, and the shoes are actually there.
segments.tr: يتحقق منطق الكمية القابلة للوعد (available-to-promise) من المخزون، ويخصصه لمركز التنفيذ في إنديانا بدلاً من مركز نيفادا — وهو أقرب إليك، وأرخص في الشحن، والأحذية موجودة فعلاً هناك.

segments.src: The **WMS** drops a pick task onto a handheld.
segments.tr: يرسل **WMS** مهمة التقاط إلى جهاز محمول.

segments.src: A picker walks a route the system optimized, scans the shelf barcode (confirming the right location), scans the shoe box (confirming the right SKU), and drops it in a tote.
segments.tr: يسير الملتقط في مسار حسّنه النظام، ويمسح باركود الرف (للتأكد من الموقع الصحيح)، ويمسح علبة الحذاء (للتأكد من الـSKU الصحيح)، ويضعها في السلة.

segments.src: Packing scans it again into a carton and prints a label.
segments.tr: تقوم التعبئة بمسحه مرة أخرى داخل كرتون وتطبع ملصقاً.

segments.src: Every one of those scans is the system asking "prove it" — that's how inventory records stay honest.
segments.tr: كل مسح من هذه المسحات هو النظام يسأل "أثبت ذلك" — وبهذا تبقى سجلات المخزون صادقة.

segments.src: The **TMS** — or the parcel-rating engine that plays its role — compares carriers and service levels for that ZIP code, picks one, and transmits the shipment data before the box is even on the trailer.
segments.tr: يقارن **TMS** — أو محرك تقييم الطرود الذي يؤدي دوره — بين الناقلين ومستويات الخدمة لذلك الرمز البريدي، ويختار أحدهم، ويرسل بيانات الشحنة قبل أن يُوضع الصندوق حتى في المقطورة.

segments.src: That's why your tracking number goes live with "label created" while the box is still sitting in Indiana.
segments.tr: ولهذا يصبح رقم التتبع الخاص بك فعالاً بعبارة "تم إنشاء الملصق" بينما ما زال الصندوق في إنديانا.

segments.src: Overnight the trailer runs to a sort hub — Memphis, Louisville, wherever the network routes it.
segments.tr: خلال الليل تنطلق المقطورة إلى مركز فرز — ممفيس أو لويزفيل، أو أي مكان توجهها إليه الشبكة.

segments.src: Each scan there is a status message flowing back upstream, which is what refreshes the tracking page you check at breakfast.
segments.tr: كل مسح هناك هو رسالة حالة تتدفق عائدة إلى الأعلى، وهي ما يحدّث صفحة التتبع التي تتفقدها على الفطور.

segments.src: Two days later it's on your porch.
segments.tr: بعد يومين تكون على شرفة منزلك.

segments.src: You saw six tracking updates.
segments.tr: رأيت ستة تحديثات للتتبع.

segments.src: The systems exchanged roughly fifty messages, and any one of them going quiet is what turns "out for delivery" into a support ticket.
segments.tr: تبادلت الأنظمة نحو خمسين رسالة، وأي واحدة منها تتوقف عن العمل هي ما يحوّل "خارج للتسليم" إلى تذكرة دعم فني.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Logistics runs on three cooperating systems: ERP (the order and the books), WMS (inside the warehouse), TMS (freight and carriers).
segments.tr: 1. تعمل اللوجستيات على ثلاثة أنظمة متعاونة: ERP (الطلب والدفاتر)، وWMS (داخل المستودع)، وTMS (الشحن والناقلون).

segments.src: 2. They talk through EDI transaction sets or APIs, and the integration seams — not the individual systems — are where most projects fail.
segments.tr: 2. تتواصل عبر مجموعات معاملات EDI أو واجهات APIs، وتكمن نقاط الربط — لا الأنظمة الفردية — حيث تفشل معظم المشاريع.

segments.src: 3. Barcodes and RFID are the data-capture layer; without accurate scans, every system downstream is confidently wrong.
segments.tr: 3. الباركود وRFID هما طبقة التقاط البيانات؛ وبدون عمليات مسح دقيقة، يكون كل نظام لاحق خاطئاً بثقة.

segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: **1.** يحتاج مركز توزيع إلى تحديد أي موقع (bin) يُخزَّن فيه البالت الوارد، وأي مسار التقاط ينبغي أن يسلكه العامل.

segments.src: Which system handles this?
segments.tr: أي نظام يتولى ذلك؟

segments.src: - A) ERP
segments.tr: - A) ERP

segments.src: - B) WMS
segments.tr: - B) WMS

segments.tr: - D) EDI

segments.tr: **2.** صح أم خطأ: الميزة الرئيسية لـ RFID على الباركود هي أن علامات RFID أرخص لكل وحدة.

segments.src: **3.** Your company is overpaying carriers because nobody checks freight invoices against contracted rates.
segments.tr: **3.** شركتك تدفع مبالغ زائدة للناقلين لأن أحداً لا يقارن فواتير الشحن بالأسعار المتعاقد عليها.

segments.src: Which capability addresses this most directly?
segments.tr: أي قدرة تعالج ذلك بشكل أكثر مباشرة؟

segments.tr: - A) الجرد الدوري في WMS

segments.tr: - B) تدقيق الشحن والدفع في TMS
